precedence_in_code.where_they_differ: Opposite order between Yahoo and the transaction median, and the script alone has the scoped-override layer. Under the Lambda a median always becomes the row for an asset that has one; under the script a Yahoo close or an override outranks it.

final_served.basis: The two served price objects the order names DISAGREE on the 2026-10-09 rows of the 34, and the served rows carry a source column, so the split is measured per object (by_served_object) and no single object is chosen here. The daily price file silver/prices/2026-10-09.parquet (one version only, written 2026-10-09T00:14:50Z, never rewritten) holds 34 of 34 as source transaction_observed with the price equal to the un-deduplicated median (0 equal the once-per-id median). The canonical_prices.parquet version first written that day (00:14:48Z) says the same. The version current at the end of that day (2026-10-09T23:03:03Z; the 23:02:48Z version agrees) holds 0 of 34 as transaction_observed: all 34 are linear_interpolation. The current version (2026-10-11T12:48:11Z) holds 28 yahoo_finance, 4 linear_interpolation and 2 transaction_observed whose price is not the median. NOT_ESTABLISHED because this read cannot say which object a consumer reads for those rows: gold B_01 load_latest_prices (lines 319-361) concatenates the canonical object and every daily file and keeps one row per asset by latest date, so the daily-file row and the canonical row of the same date tie, and the tie order was not established. No override row or Yahoo row outranked a median in the daily file or the first canonical version; the later canonical rewrites are by a writer this read could not identify (see script_path_runs_today).

held_on_served_account_day.basis: Depends on which assets are final-served, which is not established. The join itself was measured: object gold/timeseries/holdings_lots/2026-10-09.parquet (the B_01 output, one version, written 2026-10-11T05:04:51Z), column asset_name only (27 columns exist; only that one was read, by ranged reads), 1314828 rows, 11285 distinct asset keys. Joined by exact string equality of the price object's asset_name with the holdings asset_name (after whitespace strip): 159 of the 160 priced assets joined, and 34 of the 34 moved assets joined (with B_01's three-entry NAME_ALIASES applied to the price name, still 34 of 34; 1 of the 34 is an alias source name). So whichever object is taken, every one of the 34 that is final-served is held: 34 under the daily-file reading, 0 under the end-of-day canonical reading. Held here means the asset key appears in the holdings object; no account, value or quantity was read.

over_one_percent.basis: Same test as the 34. Daily file and the first canonical version of 2026-10-09: 2 of 2 final-served and 2 of 2 held (both keys appear in the holdings object). End-of-day canonical version (23:03:03Z): 0 of 2 final-served, both linear_interpolation. Current canonical version: 0 of 2 final-served (1 yahoo_finance, 1 linear_interpolation). NOT_ESTABLISHED as a single count for the same reason as final_served.

script_path_runs_today.basis: Evidence for 'only the Lambda wrote the day's daily price file': bd-price-update (state Active, last code update 2026-04-06T15:08:05Z, timeout 900) has a log stream for 2026-10-11 with first event 2026-10-11T00:18:42Z and newest event 2026-10-11T00:19:50Z, and streams for 2026-10-10 (00:18:40Z to 00:19:40Z) and 2026-10-09 (00:14:14Z to 00:15:03Z); the daily price files 2026-10-11 (00:19:28Z), 2026-10-10 (00:19:25Z) and 2026-10-09 (00:14:50Z) and the canonical versions written at 00:19:26Z, 00:19:23Z and 00:14:48Z fall inside those windows. The 2026-10-09 daily file has 106 tickered assets priced from the transaction median (Lambda order; the script would prefer a Yahoo close where one exists) and no scoped_override row although the canonical object holds scoped_override rows (the script's override layer would have written them). No EventBridge rule targets the function (list-rule-names-by-target returned nothing). The SSM document opal-bd-allocation-download (version 6, Active) is read live: it is a RETIRED no-op with no price step, so the manifest's weekday-run claim is not carried by it. Against calling the script path dead: canonical_prices.parquet is rewritten four times a day (about 04:03Z, 09:49Z, 12:47Z and 23:02Z, each a pair of writes 15 seconds apart) with no Lambda log event near them, so another writer exists whose identity was not established. NOT_ESTABLISHED because the EC2 service bd-price-runner named in infra/aws/ec2/EC2_MANIFEST.json, the SSM command history and the unidentified canonical writer were not read (ssm:ListDocuments is denied to this identity; an EC2 or SSM-history read is outside the order's reads).
